items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: he'd come and play it on the Pelican. And I was playing with P. Shawne... both bands would play against each other.

ctx.x: I see. I see. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. But they wouldn't play nothing because they had no funeral marches. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. funeral marches, and they couldn't play them. Until we meet again, there are my guard today, that's all they could play. Well it was them corner cats, they didn't want no funeral marches, they wanted some talk, you know, they didn't care about that.
Did Fayte ever come off the boat much to play jazz?

Yeah, he'd come and play it on the roof guard against us a lot of times. He'd come and play it on the Pelican. And I was playing with P. Shawne, he'd come and play a fine band. And Wilna Pfeiffer was playing with him.
